title: Jason Thomson - The Growth Factor (S2E6)

reader_summary.headline: All opinions expressed by podcast participants are solely their own opinion.
reader_summary.overview: All opinions expressed by podcast participants are solely their own opinion. and do not reflect the opinion of newfound research. My guest in this episode is Jason Thompson, a portfolio manager at the William O'Neill family office. On paper, Jason doesn't seem like a particularly good fit for this podcast.

key_points.text: He runs a highly concentrated, discretionary portfolio of growth equity names.
key_points.evidence_quote: He runs a highly concentrated, discretionary portfolio of growth equity names.

key_points.text: He can be levered long, net short, or completely out of the market, all at his discretion.
key_points.evidence_quote: He can be levered long, net short, or completely out of the market, all at his discretion.

key_points.text: What becomes rapidly apparent in our conversation, though, is that while Jason has ultimate discretion.
key_points.evidence_quote: What becomes rapidly apparent in our conversation, though, is that while Jason has ultimate discretion, he adheres closely to a disciplined rules-based process driven by the empirical research of an in-house quant group.

key_points.text: The core framework of that process retains the the spirit of William O'Neill's original CanSlim methodology.
key_points.evidence_quote: The core framework of that process retains the the spirit of William O'Neill's original CanSlim methodology, but now has nearly a half-century of learning and nuance layered on top.

thesis: The guest argues that growth investing should not be viewed as a binary opposite to value, noting that growth does not necessarily mean expensive and that temporary overvaluation can compress as earnings grow faster than expectations. He emphasizes that screening ideas strictly by value or growth buckets causes investors to miss opportunities where these two concepts converge.
